Population, matching and pay definitions

Total reported cash pay is used where available. Salary-only sources are labeled explicitly. Employer benefits are unavailable in these files, so this page cannot supply compensation including benefits. No inflation projection, trimming or composition adjustment is applied.

What the dates and departments mean

2026 person-level salary snapshots are available for Madison and Chapel Hill. Michigan, Ohio State and the three matched UC campuses have 2025 pay; Boulder has 2024. Each school always displays its latest acquired pay year, shown above.

The Berkeley, UCLA and Davis lists were checked against department websites in October 2026; each selection reports its check date. The chart uses those current ranks and memberships with the latest published payroll. It is not a complete 2026 earnings distribution: recent hires can lack a prior-year payroll match, and promotions can change rank.

Combined departments are labeled in the chart title. Population notes explain department boundaries and joint appointments. Each view shows one school and department; composition differences are documented without adjusting pay.

Economics includes joint appointments. Economics department membership can include appointments in business, law or public policy schools. Berkeley includes joint Haas business-school faculty. Reported pay can include earnings from those roles or administration; it is not isolated pay for economics teaching and research.
